note: Net migration figures come from ONS Long-term international migration (year ending December 2025, provisional, published 21 May 2026). Visa-grant figures come from Home Office Immigration system statistics (year ending March 2026). The two sources are not interchangeable: ONS counts people staying 12 months or more; the Home Office counts visas granted, which is always higher. ONS reason splits are for non-EU+ arrivals (inflow), not net migration by reason.

metrics.notes: ASYLUM APPLICANTS ONLY, 14% of non-EU+ immigration. Humanitarian is a separate ONS category, about 6%, and is NOT in this figure; family is about 7%. Labelling this bar or row 'asylum and humanitarian' understates the combined category and misstates this one. Includes those who claimed asylum after regular arrival and via illegal entry.

metrics.metric_name: Asylum applicants as a share of all long-term immigration (calculated)
metrics.source_name: Calculated from ONS Long-term international migration, provisional: year ending December 2025 (Tables 1 and 4b)
metrics.notes: Calculated by this project: 88,000 asylum-related long-term immigration, ONS Table 4b, divided by 813,000 total long-term immigration, ONS Table 1, both provisional and both year ending December 2025, is 10.82%, shown here as 10.8%. ONS PUBLISHES ITS REASON BREAKDOWN AGAINST NON-EU+ ARRIVALS ONLY and states no share of all immigration, which is why this is derived rather than read off a release. Both inputs are rounded to the nearest thousand by ONS and the share holds at 10.8% across the whole rounding interval, 10.76% to 10.89%, so the rounding does not reach the published digit. ASYLUM APPLICANTS ONLY, on the same basis as the numerator: humanitarian is a separate ONS category and is not in it. The companion figure is the 14% share of non-EU+ arrivals, the same numerator over a smaller denominator, which is the framing ONS itself uses.
